assets.prompt: An illustrated 1980s field-service handbook laid open flat on a workbench as a single isolated object viewed in three-quarter axonometric perspective. Wide double-page spread slightly angled, ivory thick pages with gently fanned curved edges, three dark metal binder rings, ink blue cloth cover, narrow cream chapter tabs on right edge. Left page: one precise small exploded-view line drawing of a bench instrument module, right page: three checkboxes with short horizontal lines and a small printed wiring diagram. An understated technical pencil lies in the gutter. No legible text, lettering, numbers, no logo, no birds. Engraved charcoal fine keylines, warm silver fasteners, subtle flat two-tone shading, quiet almost monochrome graphic with only desaturated ink blue; the drawing belongs in the same vintage engineering manual as the test equipment. Balanced composition with ample breathing room, fully isolated on a transparent background for dark or light use. Landscape 3:2. No desk surface, no background, no scene dressing, no floating objects, no gradients, no decorative shadows or photographic lighting.

A self contained tabletop dual-channel strip chart recorder as drawn in a 1983 electronics service manual. A hinged light ivory/aluminium case open at a three-quarter angle, two pens side by side leave one short square pulse on the top trace and a delayed pulse on the lower trace on a single wide ribbon of cream graph paper emerging towards the viewer, representing an HTTP request followed by a Kafka event. Two blue-black coaxial sockets behind the paper. Distinctive low horizontal profile, paper and rollers are the focus, no terminal screen, no keyboards. Fine deliberate charcoal ink outlines, warm bone painted metal, screws, lighter bevels, neatly drawn fine linework, lightly textured flat engineering illustration, restrained desaturated blue ink on traces. Isolated entirely on transparent background, generous outer margins, 3:2 landscape. No labels, no letters, no branding, no birds, no green, no gradients, no backdrop, no extra objects. Clear bold silhouette legible at 300px on dark or light websites.

A single compact optical print comparator, a charming analog instrument used to compare an intended drawing with the measured result, for an illustrated 1980s electronics service manual. Landscape 3:2 isolated transparent cutout. Top-front three-quarter axonometric view. A low broad warm-ivory metal base and a hinged transparent glass plate above an off-white ruled paper drawing. Two closely aligned traces run from left to right across the plate, graphite solid line on the paper and restrained blue line etched on the glass; they coincide at first and visibly diverge by one grid interval on the right. One small round magnifying loupe in a brushed-steel arm makes the difference clearly legible, one knurled adjustment wheel. Fine intentional charcoal outlines, expertly drafted components and sparse crosshatching, satin aluminum details, a little slate blue, the look of a tactile technical manual illustration. Keep all of the instrument in frame with comfortable margins. No letters, text, brand, animals, green accents, title, badges, screen, printer, sci-fi styling, large shadows or tabletop background.

Create one finished wide landscape editorial illustration for the test repository section of an elegant software product site. The first reference is the exact Falcon software document which will be inserted by a compositor into the art. The second shows the hand-drafted instrument/physical-material art style. Design a beautiful physical document folio for a reliability engineer on a pale lavender-gray studio background, drawn like a high-end Japanese technical stationery ad. Camera perfectly straight overhead, orthographic, zero perspective skew. In the left and central area sits a single big front-facing empty flat white landscape proof sheet with a 16:10 ratio. The sheet is perfectly level to the horizontal/vertical edges of the main canvas. Absolutely blank pure white interior, as a slot for the supplied unaltered screen. The slot must be entirely visible and unobstructed: place the graphite metal spring clip strictly ABOVE the proof sheet's white interior on its mount, never on the page. Stack below the white sheet two muted ivory and deep French-blue folder leaves (their corners visible, no more leaves). Restrain the surrounding details to one translucent dusty-rose tab on its right and a small well-drawn dark drafting pencil lying beside the folio. Gentle paper and aluminium textures, fine black contour lines, light at top left, short clean shadows, excellent tactile detail. White proof area takes about 60% of the canvas width and at least 53% of canvas height; sufficient outside space for all props. Light lavender-gray background extends smoothly to every edge, no borders. All objects 100% visible in frame with comfortable breathing room. No giant floating cards, no model lettering, no reproduced screenshot, no symbols or typography added, no green, no checkboxes, no logo, no people, no birds; no gradients or neon. One composition. 3:2 landscape.

One precise landscape illustration for Falcon's API Testing workbench website. The first reference is a REAL Kafka software screen that a compositor will later insert intact; reserve one completely blank off-white 16:10 screen aperture. The second is an approved warm ivory technical-manual instrument that defines the rendering style. Create a distinctly different, wide 1980s benchtop protocol analyzer on a soft cool blue-gray studio surface. Front panel is drawn in flat front elevation square to camera, so the single wide completely white 16:10 display at left and center is a perfect axis-aligned rectangle, unobstructed, and at least 53% of the canvas width. Keep actual empty display pure white and without marks/text/data, framed with a thin dark charcoal gasket. At right on the same panel, a slim vertical column with two matching navy BNC plugs and ONE round fine calibration dial. Two short lead wires emerge at the right, turn in gentle arcs and plug into a little dual-trace graphite-and-pale-amber signal probe parked beside the instrument. All leads terminate visibly. A small amount of casing thickness is visible beneath; the display remains unskewed. Weighted warm ivory powder-coated metal, four screws, two low rubber feet, engraved graphite linework and a desaturated blue top lip. Precise plausible Industrial Design editorial drawing, not a hyperreal 3D mockup. It should feel solid and compact, not a laptop or conventional monitor. Strong silhouette. Subtle contact shadows. Wide 3:2 layout, generous margins around every object, cohesive cool muted background covering the full image to its edges. No fake text, no scene title, no gradients, no bird logos or people or green; no additional sheets, no hands, no shadowy room.
